name: Chopper
description: Filtering and trimming of long reads (FASTQ or unaligned BAM).

inputs.name: input
inputs.label: Reads to filter
inputs.help: FASTQ or unaligned BAM (e.g. as produced by dorado).

inputs.name: contam
inputs.label: Reference FASTA
inputs.help: FASTA file with reference to check potential contaminants against.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.label: Minimal quality score
parameters.help: Sets a minimum Phred average quality score.

parameters.name: maxqual
parameters.label: Maximal quality score
parameters.help: Sets a maximum Phred average quality score.

parameters.name: minlength
parameters.label: Sets a minimum read length
parameters.help: Minimal length of read to keep.

parameters.name: maxlength
parameters.label: Sets a maximum read length
parameters.help: Maximal length of read to keep

parameters.name: mingc
parameters.label: Minimum GC content
parameters.help: Sets a minimum GC content for reads to keep.

parameters.name: maxgc
parameters.label: Maximum GC content
parameters.help: Sets a maximum GC content for reads to keep.

test_parameter.name: trim_approach
test_parameter.label: Trimming approach
test_parameter.help: Trimming is applied after quality/length filtering. Leave as 'No trimming' to disable.

options.label: Fixed crop (remove a fixed number of bases from read ends)
Trim by quality (trim low-quality bases from both ends)
Best read segment (keep the highest-quality segment of each read)
Split by low quality (split reads at low-quality stretches)

parameters.name: headcrop
parameters.label: Head crop
parameters.help: Trim this many nucleotides from the start of each read.

parameters.name: tailcrop
parameters.label: Tail crop
parameters.help: Trim this many nucleotides from the end of each read.

parameters.name: cutoff
parameters.label: Quality cutoff (Q-score)
parameters.help: Bases below this Phred quality at the read ends are trimmed until a base meets the cutoff.

parameters.name: cutoff
parameters.label: Quality cutoff (Q-score)
parameters.help: Minimum per-base Phred quality used to extract the highest-quality segment of each read.

parameters.name: cutoff
parameters.label: Quality cutoff (Q-score)
parameters.help: Stretches of bases below this Phred quality are treated as low-quality split points.

parameters.name: split_window
parameters.label: Split window
parameters.help: Minimum number of consecutive sub-cutoff bases required to split a read.

test_parameter.name: trim_poly_tails_select
test_parameter.label: Trim poly(A) tails and poly(T) heads

parameters.name: trim_poly_tails
parameters.label: Minimum poly(A)/poly(T) length
parameters.help: Removes a poly(T) head and a poly(A) tail of at least this length (up to 20% other bases allowed) that reach the read end. Remove adapters and primers first. Applied after the trimming approach above.

parameters.name: update_mods
parameters.label: Update base modification tags
parameters.help: Recompute MM/ML/MN tags so they match the trimmed read. Requires unaligned BAM input, or FASTQ written with 'samtools fastq -T MM,ML,MN'.

parameters.name: inverse
parameters.label: Output the opposite of the normal results
parameters.help: Reverse the output results (aka, the 'failed reads')

help.content:
**Chopper**

Rust implementation of NanoFilt+NanoLyse, both originally written in Python. This tool, intended for long read sequencing such as PacBio or ONT, filters and trims a FASTQ or unaligned BAM file (such as the default output of dorado).
Filtering is done on average read quality, minimal or maximal read length, and GC content, while printing the reads passing the filter.

**Input and output formats**

By default the output has the same format as the input. Use *Output format* to convert between them:

- BAM to FASTQ writes every BAM tag as a tab-separated SAM field after the read name (like ``samtools fastq -T '*'``).
- FASTQ to BAM turns such fields back into typed tags.
- BAM to BAM keeps the input header and all tags, adding a ``@PG`` line.

Aligned, secondary, supplementary or paired BAM records are rejected.

**Trimming**

Trimming is opt-in via the *Trimming approach* selector and is applied after the filtering steps. Choose one of:

- **Fixed crop** (``--trim-approach fixed-crop``): remove a fixed number of bases from the start (``--headcrop``) and/or end (``--tailcrop``) of each read.
- **Trim by quality** (``--trim-approach trim-by-quality``): trim low-quality bases from both ends until a base with quality ≥ the ``--cutoff`` Q-score is reached.
- **Best read segment** (``--trim-approach best-read-segment``): keep only the highest-quality segment of each read, based on ``--cutoff``.
- **Split by low quality** (``--trim-approach split-by-low-quality``): split reads at low-quality stretches and output the high-quality parts. A read is only split once a run of consecutive sub-``--cutoff`` bases reaches the ``--split-window`` length (default 1); shorter dips are tolerated and kept inside the segment, while leading and trailing low-quality bases are still trimmed.

**Additional trimming**

- **Poly(A)/poly(T) trimming** (``--trim-poly-tails``): removes a poly(T) head and a poly(A) tail of at least the given length, allowing up to 20% other bases. Tails must reach the read end, so remove adapters and primers first. It is applied after the trimming approach above.
- **Update base modification tags** (``--update-mods``): recomputes MM/ML/MN tags so the modification calls still match the trimmed read.

Compared to the Python implementation the scope is to deliver the same results, almost the same functionality, at much faster execution times. At the moment this tool does not support filtering using a sequencing_summary file.

**More Information** 

- **Official Repository**: `Chopper on GitHub`_

.. _Chopper on GitHub: https://github.com/wdecoster/chopper
